classification.difficultyReason: Represent the angle bisectors, infer equal base angles from AB=AC, and halve them to obtain equal angles in triangle BXC; the isosceles converse then gives XB=XC.

content.prompt: In the triangle $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$. The bisectors of angles $ABC$ and $ACB$ meet at $X$. Prove that $XB=XC$.

answer.worked:
$AB=AC$, so $\angle ABC=\angle ACB$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle). Since $BX$ and $CX$ bisect these angles:
$$\begin{align*}\angle CBX&=\angle BCX &&\text{(halves of equal angles)}\\\angle BCX&=\angle CBX &&\text{(same equality)}\\BC&=CB &&\text{(common side)}\end{align*}$$
Thus $\triangle BCX\equiv\triangle CBX$ (AAS), with $B$ corresponding to $C$. Therefore $XB=XC$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
